version_bodies.title: KIP-1308: Extend Header API for Common Value Types

storage.value:
Status

Current state: Voting

Discussion thread: Link

Voting thread: Link

JIRA: ASF JIRA5aa69414-a9e9-3523-82ec-879b028fb15bKAFKA-20387

Please keep the discussion on the mailing list rather than commenting on the wiki (wiki discussions get unwieldy fast).

Motivation

RecordHeader stores its value as byte[]. This is the right wire representation, but it makes the API challenging for the types everyone mostly puts in headers (string, int, boolean...):

Construction is tedious:

java

Reading is tedious:

java

Keys and values on ProducerRecord have configurable serializers. Headers have nothing -- every team writes their own wrappers (LoggableRecordHeader, utility methods, byte constants) to make headers usable.

Public Interfaces

 New default methods on Header and Headers in org.apache.kafka.common.header. There are no new classes or configs, and the wire format does not change.

javaHeader.javaIt is the caller's responsibility to ensure the value was originally stored as a string with the * matching charset. * * @param charset the charset to use for decoding. * @return the header's value decoded as a string. * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the header's value is null. */ default String stringValue(Charset charset) { return new String(nonNullValue(), charset); } /** * Returns the header's value interpreted as a boolean, where {@code 0x01} is {@code true} and {@code 0x00} * is {@code false}. * *

It is the caller's responsibility to ensure the value was originally stored as a boolean. * * @return the header's value as a boolean. * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the header's value is null, is not exactly 1 byte, or is neither * {@code 0x00} nor {@code 0x01}. */ default boolean booleanValue() { byte b = nonNullValue(1)[0]; if (b != 0 && b != 1) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Header '" + key() + "' value " + b + " is not a boolean"); return b == 1; } /** * Returns the header's value as a single byte. * *

It is the caller's responsibility to ensure the value was originally stored as a byte. * * @return the header's value as a byte. * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the header's value is null or is not exactly 1 byte. */ default byte byteValue() { return nonNullValue(Byte.BYTES)[0]; } /** * Returns the header's value interpreted as a big-endian short. * *

It is the caller's responsibility to ensure the value was originally stored as a short. * * @return the header's value as a short. * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the header's value is null or is not exactly 2 bytes. */ default short shortValue() { return ByteBuffer.wrap(nonNullValue(Short.BYTES)).getShort(); } /** * Returns the header's value interpreted as a big-endian int. * *

It is the caller's responsibility to ensure the value was originally stored as an int. * * @return the header's value as an int. * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the header's value is null or is not exactly 4 bytes. */ default int intValue() { return ByteBuffer.wrap(nonNullValue(Integer.BYTES)).getInt(); } /** * Returns the header's value interpreted as a big-endian long. * *

It is the caller's responsibility to ensure the value was originally stored as a long. * * @return the header's value as a long. * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the header's value is null or is not exactly 8 bytes. */ default long longValue() { return ByteBuffer.wrap(nonNullValue(Long.BYTES)).getLong(); } /** * Returns the header's value interpreted as a big-endian IEEE 754 float. * *

It is the caller's responsibility to ensure the value was originally stored as a float. * * @return the header's value as a float. * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the header's value is null or is not exactly 4 bytes. */ default float floatValue() { return ByteBuffer.wrap(nonNullValue(Float.BYTES)).getFloat(); } /** * Returns the header's value interpreted as a big-endian IEEE 754 double. * *

It is the caller's responsibility to ensure the value was originally stored as a double. * * @return the header's value as a double. * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the header's value is null or is not exactly 8 bytes. */ default double doubleValue() { return ByteBuffer.wrap(nonNullValue(Double.BYTES)).getDouble(); } private byte[] nonNullValue() { byte[] v = value(); if (v == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Header '" + key() + "' has a null value"); return v; } private byte[] nonNullValue(int size) { byte[] v = nonNullValue(); if (v.length != size) throw new IllegalArgumentException( "Header '" + key() + "' value has " + v.length + " bytes, expected " + size); return v; } }]]>


javaHeaders.java {      /** * Creates and adds a header with a boolean value, to the end, returning if the operation succeeded. * * @param key of the header to be added; must not be null. * @param value of the header to be added. * @return this instance of the Headers, once the header is added. * @throws IllegalStateException is thrown if headers are in a read-only state. */ default Headers addBoolean(String key, boolean value) throws IllegalStateException { return add(key, new byte[]{(byte) (value ? 1 : 0)}); } /** * Creates and adds a header with a byte value, to the end, returning if the operation succeeded. * * @param key of the header to be added; must not be null. * @param value of the header to be added. * @return this instance of the Headers, once the header is added. * @throws IllegalStateException is thrown if headers are in a read-only state. */ default Headers addByte(String key, byte value) throws IllegalStateException { return add(key, new byte[]{value}); } /** * Creates and adds a header with a string value encoded using the given charset, to the end, returning if the * operation succeeded. * * @param key of the header to be added; must not be null. * @param value of the header to be added; may be null. * @param charset the charset to use for encoding the string value. * @return this instance of the Headers, once the header is added. * @throws IllegalStateException is thrown if headers are in a read-only state. */ default Headers addString(String key, String value, Charset charset) throws IllegalStateException { return add(key, value == null ? null : value.getBytes(charset)); } /** * Creates and adds a header with a short value, to the end, returning if the operation succeeded. * * @param key of the header to be added; must not be null. * @param value of the header to be added. * @return this instance of the Headers, once the header is added. * @throws IllegalStateException is thrown if headers are in a read-only state. */ default Headers addShort(String key, short value) throws IllegalStateException { return add(key, ByteBuffer.allocate(Short.BYTES).putShort(value).array()); } /** * Creates and adds a header with an int value, to the end, returning if the operation succeeded. * * @param key of the header to be added; must not be null. * @param value of the header to be added. * @return this instance of the Headers, once the header is added. * @throws IllegalStateException is thrown if headers are in a read-only state. */ default Headers addInt(String key, int value) throws IllegalStateException { return add(key, ByteBuffer.allocate(Integer.BYTES).putInt(value).array()); } /** * Creates and adds a header with a long value, to the end, returning if the operation succeeded. * * @param key of the header to be added; must not be null. * @param value of the header to be added. * @return this instance of the Headers, once the header is added. * @throws IllegalStateException is thrown if headers are in a read-only state. */ default Headers addLong(String key, long value) throws IllegalStateException { return add(key, ByteBuffer.allocate(Long.BYTES).putLong(value).array()); } /** * Creates and adds a header with a float value, to the end, returning if the operation succeeded. * * @param key of the header to be added; must not be null. * @param value of the header to be added. * @return this instance of the Headers, once the header is added. * @throws IllegalStateException is thrown if headers are in a read-only state. */ default Headers addFloat(String key, float value) throws IllegalStateException { return add(key, ByteBuffer.allocate(Float.BYTES).putFloat(value).array()); } /** * Creates and adds a header with a double value, to the end, returning if the operation succeeded. * * @param key of the header to be added; must not be null. * @param value of the header to be added. * @return this instance of the Headers, once the header is added. * @throws IllegalStateException is thrown if headers are in a read-only state. */ default Headers addDouble(String key, double value) throws IllegalStateException { return add(key, ByteBuffer.allocate(Double.BYTES).putDouble(value).array()); }     // rest of the methods }]]>

Proposed Changes

Header gains default typed accessors that decode value(). Headers gains default typed add methods that encode the value and call the existing add(String, byte[]), so read-only checks apply the same way like any other add. Every existing implementation, including the ones that ship with the clients, inherits the new methods without changes.

Null handling: ofString(key, null, charset) (ofStringUtf8) and ofBytes(key, null) create a header with a null byte[] value, consistent with the existing RecordHeader(String, byte[]) constructor which accepts null. Primitive factories (ofInt, ofLong, etc.) cannot accept null since they take primitives. 

Each deserializes the internal byte[]. Throws IllegalStateException if the byte array is the wrong size for the requested type (e.g. calling intValue() on a 7-byte array). Calling a typed accessor on a header with a null value throws IllegalStateException. stringValue() on a null value returns null. addString(key, null, charset) adds a header with a null value, as add(key, null) does today. Applications that need another encoding, such as little-endian integers, keep using value() and add(String, byte[]).

Compatibility, Deprecation, and Migration Plan

The change is source and binary compatible. The new methods are defaults on Header and Headers, so existing implementations compile and run unchanged, and the wire format does not change. An implementation that already declares one of the new signatures overrides the default. If its return type differs, for example an addInt that returns void, it no longer compiles and must rename that method.

Nothing is deprecated, and no migration is required.

Test Plan

  • Unit tests run every typed add and accessor against minimal Header and Headers implementations that implement only the abstract methods.
  • Unit test checks that typed adds on read-only headers throw IllegalStateException.

Rejected Alternatives

Abstract methods on Header and Headers. Every third-party implementation would stop compiling on upgrade, only to gain methods that behave the same for every implementation

Static factories on RecordHeader, such as RecordHeader.ofInt(key, value). RecordHeader lives in an internals package outside the public API. Typed adds on Headers serve the same callers without making an internal class.

Configurable header serde on producer/consumer. A config mapping header keys to serializer classes adds complexity and couples header semantics to client config. The common types (string, int, long, short, float, double, boolean) cover the vast majority of header usage and don't need configuration.

Generic serde parameter stored on RecordHeader instance. new RecordHeader(key, value, serializer) makes RecordHeader serde-aware and stores extra references. The static factory approach keeps RecordHeader as a (String, byte[]) tuple with no new instance state. The generic of() / value() methods accept a class, instantiate it, use it, and discard it.

Moving ReadcordHeader/RecordHeaders as part of the public API. Moving the classes out of the internals will break compatibility and force a major version change. The default implementation since the inception of the classes has been within the internals package. We aim to preserve this design choice.

Proposed Changes

While RecordHeader is defined under the internals/ package, the public class access is not preventing users from creating a reference via the RecordHeader class. To properly support types, we add new overloaded methods on Header and Headers.

Each ofXXX method serializes the value to byte[] internally using the same encoding as the corresponding Kafka Serializer (UTF-8 for strings, big-endian for numerics, single byte 0x01/0x00 for boolean).

javaRecordHeader

Typed Accessors

java

Same pattern: instantiate, deserialize, discard.

The existing byte[] value() method is unchanged.

Null handling: ofString(key, null, charset) (ofStringUtf8) and ofBytes(key, null) create a header with a null byte[] value, consistent with the existing RecordHeader(String, byte[]) constructor which accepts null. Primitive factories (ofInt, ofLong, etc.) cannot accept null since they take primitives. 

Each deserializes the internal byte[]. Throws IllegalStateException if the byte array is the wrong size for the requested type (e.g. calling intValue() on a 7-byte array). Calling a typed accessor on a header with a null value throws IllegalStateException. stringValue() on a null value returns null.

Compatibility, Deprecation, and Migration Plan

Fully backward compatible. All changes are additive with new static factories and new accessor methods. Existing RecordHeader(String, byte[]) constructor and byte[] value() are unchanged. 

Test Plan

  • Unit tests for each static factory (ofString, ofInt, ofLong, ofShort, ofFloat, ofDouble, ofBoolean, ofBytes)
  • Unit tests for each typed accessor, including wrong-size byte array errors
  • Unit tests for wrong-type reading (e.g. create with ofInt, read with stringValue())
  • Unit tests for null values - ofString(key, null), ofBytes(key, null), and typed accessor on null value
  • Unit tests for boundary values (Integer.MAX_VALUE, Integer.MIN_VALUE, Long.MAX_VALUE, Double.NaN, Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY, etc.)
  • Unit tests for empty string (ofString(key, ""))
  • Unit tests for Unicode strings (multi-byte characters, emojis)
  • Unit tests verifying byte[] value() is unchanged
  • Integration tests verifying headers created with static factories survive produce/consume round-trip
  • Integration tests verifying typed accessors work on headers received from consumer

Rejected Alternatives

Configurable header serde on producer/consumer. A config mapping header keys to serializer classes adds complexity and couples header semantics to client config. The common types (string, int, long, short, float, double, boolean) cover the vast majority of header usage and don't need configuration.

Default methods on the Header/Headers interface. While this will help avoid compilation errors after upgrading to a newer AK version, it is better than silently failing for implementers. If users roll their own version of record headers, they must be aware of the type-aware methods and consciously adapt it to their use cases.

Generic serde parameter stored on RecordHeader instance. new RecordHeader(key, value, serializer) makes RecordHeader serde-aware and stores extra references. The static factory approach keeps RecordHeader as a (String, byte[]) tuple with no new instance state. The generic of() / value() methods accept a class, instantiate it, use it, and discard it.

Moving ReadcordHeader/RecordHeaders as part of the public API. Moving the classes out of the internals will break compatibility and force a major version change. The default implementation since the inception of the classes has been within the internals package. We aim to preserve this design choice.
